title: Productize stable personal-content authoring, ingestion, migration, and canonical metadata

scope.subject: Astro Content Collections authoring pipeline for stable personal content identity, localization, mapping metadata, migration, validation, and deterministic import

research_summary: Keep Astro Content Collections as the canonical repository-backed content source and add only a deterministic project-owned authoring/validation adapter around it. The existing collection already supplies local file loading, Zod validation, typed collection queries, and static build integration, so a CMS would duplicate authority and add administration/auth/runtime surface. The implementation will store stable content IDs explicitly, preserve one bilingual identity, expose destination/discovery/Surface metadata without creating parallel universe models, and use a small Node CLI for scaffolding, JSON batch ingestion, migration, preview, and asset/reference checks.

sources.finding: Astro Content Collections already provide repository-local Markdown/MDX/data loading, schema validation, and typed collection queries, covering the canonical source and build integration without a second database.
Keystatic can add a Git/local editing UI on top of repository content, but it introduces an editor/admin layer that is unnecessary while direct repository authoring remains cheap and deterministic.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keystatic is a credible complete authoring UI, but it is broader than the current need and would add packages and an admin surface before repository authoring is proven insufficient.
The existing Astro framework already owns build-time content loading and validation, so the pipeline should stay inside that framework instead of adding another application runtime.
Astro Content Collections cover the canonical content subsystem; only project-specific stable identity, cross-record integrity, mapping metadata, migration, and authoring ergonomics remain.
Astro's existing Zod-backed schema plus Node standard-library file/crypto primitives are sufficient for deterministic scaffolding and validation, so no parser/CLI dependency is required.

candidates.name: Existing Astro Content Collections plus narrow deterministic repository authoring helpers
candidates.source: Current src/content.config.ts, Astro Content Collections, and repository-local Node tooling
candidates.reason: Preserves the accepted canonical source, schema validation, typed collection loading, static performance, and Git history while requiring only small project-specific helpers for stable identity and integrity.

candidates.name: Keystatic repository-backed authoring CMS
candidates.reason: It would improve GUI editing but adds editor packages, configuration, and an admin workflow without replacing the existing Astro canonical data model or solving destination/Surface mapping automatically.

decision.rationale: Reuse the already-installed Astro Content Collections subsystem and keep authoring as a thin deterministic repository workflow. This minimizes maintenance and runtime surface while still allowing explicit stable IDs, bilingual metadata, deterministic mapping hints, migration/versioning, batch ingestion, asset/reference validation, and future optional editors over the same files.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: The full CMS is broader but loses globally at current scale because it adds packages and an admin/editing surface while canonical validation, repository persistence, and content loading already exist; destination and universe-specific integrity still require the same project adapter.

decision.fallback: If direct repository authoring becomes the dominant maintenance cost, add Keystatic later as an editor over the same canonical collection rather than replacing the content source or universe mapping contracts.
